title: Pathway map of the reasoning library
source: docs/program/evidence/library-pathways/model-brief.md (sections 12, 13 and 14, revisions 2 to 4, override the earlier sections)
note: One description of the model. The engine computes from it and the page draws from it. It maps and measures; it proposes no fixes.
unit: One piece of work: a fix-sized task of about ten cheap calls, where a result is produced and checked.
period: One period is 30 days. The number of periods is a run setting: it is chosen, never drawn and never swung.
cost_unit: Cheap-call equivalents. One call by the cheap model (Sonnet) costs 1. Lookup, screen, carry and handoff are paid at the cheap tier.
revision_note: Revision 2: a good entry shortens the cheap attempt (s_exact, s_similar, s_comp, s_part); coverage of work the cheap model gets right alone is scaled by ok_coverage_factor; only strong-tier solves that pass the gate are stored, and a strong-tier escape that passes writes a bad entry; a found escape's bad entry is corrected with fix_on_found; the cheap retry goes through the same gate.
revision_3_note: Revision 3 follows brief section 13. The Opus price ratio is an unknown from 1 to 2. Coverage counts every stored entry, good or bad. Each period a share of bad entries leaves the stock (retire_bad). Every unknown has a side; a library-side unknown also has a good end. The ensemble can tie the library-side draws together. There are three reference settings. The funnel is declared below as measures. The weight of a limitation measures how much it holds the result down.
revision_4_note: Revision 4 follows brief section 14. Library-side unknowns fall into four groups: comes back, reach, entry quality and running cost. The reference settings are the middle values, the eight corners of three groups, the all-good setting and the worst corner. Tied draws use four shared levels, one per group. Two weights, alone and last, are shares of the full fall. The gate and the ladder are shared groups, shown in their own table. Checks promoted into the shared test run are a new pathway: they act at the gate with no lookup.
todays_notes: Today's notes are CLAUDE.md, the memory notes and the checks in the shared test run. They are present in every way of working, so they cancel out. The chance that the cheap model alone is wrong describes it as it works today, with those notes. The coverage ceilings mean what the library could hold beyond today's notes.

stocks.update_note: Each period is evaluated on the stocks at its start; then both stocks are updated together from those starting values. New entries are the flows through the drawn write branches; a repair moves one entry from bad to good. Only Opus and Fable outputs that pass the gate are written; cheap-tier outputs never are. A share retire_bad of the bad entries at the start of the period leaves the stock (revision 3).

update.same_as: E_good - delta_stale * E_good + episodes_per_period * (P_strong_right * w_write * e_right + P_strong_escaped * l_found * w_write * fix_on_found)

update.expr: E_bad - retire_bad * E_bad + delta_stale * E_good + episodes_per_period * (W_bad_right + W_bad_escape - W_repair)
update.same_as: E_bad - retire_bad * E_bad + delta_stale * E_good + episodes_per_period * (P_strong_right * w_write * (1 - e_right) + P_strong_escaped * w_write - P_strong_escaped * l_found * w_write * fix_on_found)

funnel_note: Brief section 13, R16. Each stage is a flow through states or branches of this graph, for the library policy at one period. Each stage is part of the one before it. A wrong entry that comes back is counted at the third stage and leaves at the fourth. A look-alike that comes back is not the right entry. Checks promoted into the shared tests do not pass through this funnel. Their measure is promo_measure (revision 4, R21).

reference_settings_note: Brief section 14, R18a. A group at poor has every unknown at its poor end. A group at good has every unknown at its good end. A level may also be a number from 0 to 1, a quantile counted from the poor end. A group not named stays at its middle values. Other-side unknowns always stay at their middle values. The corners leave running cost at its middle values. all_good_costly is declared for the page: the all-good setting with running cost at its high end. The funnel shows one faint mark, at funnel_mark.

sheets.label: Middle value of how much comes back

square.note: Brief section 14, R18c. Reach runs across and entry quality up, in eleven levels from the poor end (0) to the good end (1). A level is a quantile of each unknown's range, counted from its poor end, as in the tied draws. Each sheet fixes how much comes back: little, the middle value or much. Running cost and other-side unknowns stay at their middle values. Each cell gives the four ratios at the last period.

variants.label: The same settings, with the Opus price ratio at one

variants_note: A variant is a parameter set with some values replaced. The page and the record show only the variants declared here. opus_one: the price list gives 2 per token; per call the ratio may be nearer 1 (revision 3, R10).

ensemble_ties.note: Brief section 14, R18b. Each run draws four shared levels, one per group, in the order of lib_groups. They come from a stream kept apart from the own draws. A library-side unknown sits at tie times its group's level plus (1 - tie) times its own draw. Both are counted from its poor end. No group is tied to another. Tie 0 is the untied draw, the same as revision 3, draw for draw. Other unknowns are always drawn on their own. The three unknowns of R21 come from a third stream.

weight.note: Brief section 14, R19. The score of a setting is the mean fall in the library's cost and wrong rate from the middle values. The full fall is the score of the all-good setting. For a set of library-side unknowns, alone is the score with only that set at its good ends. Last is the full fall less the score of the all-good setting with that set back at its middle values. Both are shares of the full fall. Alone can be below zero and last above one. The shares do not add up, because the steps multiply. Other-side unknowns stay at their middle values. A limitation that acts only through other-side unknowns has no weight on this measure. If those unknowns belong to the gate or the ladder, the shared table shows them.

shared_groups.label: The ladder: retry, Opus, Fable and the handoff

shared_table.note: Brief section 14, R20. These unknowns act in all three ways of working, so the weight gives them none. Each group moves together to the end shown. The table gives cost and wrong rate of the three ways. It does so at the middle values and at the all-good setting. Each is shown as it is, with the gate moved, with the ladder moved, and with both.

links_note: A link is an influence on branch chances that is not a step of a piece of work. promoted_checks: in the library way of working, an entry's mechanical check can also run in the shared tests. It needs no lookup, so it does not pass through the funnel. It can only raise the gate's catch chance, at every gate pass: g_lib = g + (1 - g) * promo. That equals 1 - (1 - g) * (1 - promo). It acts on exact and similar entries, weighed by the share of good entries. Left out: a bad entry's promoted check can pin a defect in place. Leaving it out leans toward the library.
limitations_note: Filled in after the real-case walkthroughs. Each entry will name a limitation and the parameters it acts through; each branch carries the ids of the limitations that act on it.
